concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate limits of functions, determine the existence of limits, and use limit properties to analyze function behavior.
concepts.name: Limits
concepts.description: The concept of a limit defines the value that a function approaches as its input approaches a specific point, forming the foundation for continuity, differentiation, and integration.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to test a function for continuity at a point, identify discontinuities, and understand the relationship between continuity and differentiability.
concepts.name: Continuity
concepts.description: A function is continuous at a point if the limit at that point equals the function's value there; continuity is a prerequisite for differentiability and ensures no abrupt changes in the function.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute derivatives using limit definitions, apply differentiation rules, and interpret the derivative as a slope of the tangent line.
concepts.name: Derivatives
concepts.description: The derivative of a function measures the instantaneous rate of change of the function with respect to its input, formally defined as a limit of difference quotients.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute partial derivatives, understand their geometric interpretation, and apply them in multivariable calculus contexts.
concepts.name: Partial Derivatives
concepts.description: Partial derivatives extend differentiation to functions of several variables, measuring the rate of change with respect to one variable while holding the others constant.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to analyze the domain, range, and behavior of single-variable functions and understand them as the basis for calculus operations.
concepts.name: Functions of One Variable
concepts.description: Real-valued functions defined on subsets of the real numbers, serving as the fundamental mathematical objects upon which differential and integral calculus operations are performed.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate limits analytically, understand the formal epsilon-delta definition, and apply limit laws to determine the behavior of functions at specific points and at infinity.
concepts.name: Limits of Functions
concepts.description: The foundational concept of calculus describing the value that a function approaches as the input approaches some point, essential for defining continuity, derivatives, and integrals rigorously.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute derivatives using various techniques, interpret derivatives as rates of change and slopes, and apply differentiation to solve optimization and related rates problems.
concepts.name: Differential Calculus
concepts.description: The study of rates of change and the slopes of curves through the concept of the derivative, including differentiation rules, techniques, and applications to optimization and curve sketching.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate definite and indefinite integrals, apply integration techniques, understand the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, and calculate areas and accumulated quantities.
concepts.name: Integral Calculus
concepts.description: The study of accumulation, antiderivatives, and the area under curves through definite and indefinite integrals, including the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connecting integration with differentiation.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to formulate mathematical models of physical situations using calculus, solve applied problems involving motion and change, and connect abstract calculus concepts to concrete scientific and engineering examples.
concepts.name: Applications of Calculus to Science and Engineering
concepts.description: The practical implementation of differential and integral calculus to model and analyze physical phenomena including change, motion, growth, and accumulation in scientific and engineering contexts.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to recognize properties of functions and their inverses, describe domain and range, and work with polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, and inverse-trigonometric functions.
concepts.name: Functions and Their Properties
concepts.description: Study of various function types including polynomials, rational functions, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, and inverse-trigonometric functions, with emphasis on identifying domains, ranges, and inverse relationships.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to identify indeterminate forms and apply appropriate techniques to evaluate limits that initially appear undefined.
concepts.name: Indeterminate Forms and Limit Evaluation
concepts.description: Techniques for resolving indeterminate forms such as 0/0, ∞/∞, 0·∞, ∞−∞, 0⁰, 1^∞, and ∞⁰ that arise when evaluating limits, including algebraic manipulation and special methods.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to understand continuity of a function and its properties, identify continuous functions from their graphs, and analyze discontinuous functions.
concepts.name: Continuity of Functions
concepts.description: Analysis of continuous and discontinuous functions, conditions for continuity at a point, types of discontinuities, and applications of continuous functions in modeling real-world phenomena.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to define tangent lines and rates of change and relate these concepts with the derivative of a function.
concepts.name: Derivative as Rate of Change
concepts.description: The fundamental interpretation of the derivative as measuring instantaneous rate of change, with geometric meaning as slope of tangent line and physical applications to motion and change.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to know and apply techniques to find derivatives of a function including product rule, quotient rule, chain rule, and implicit differentiation.
concepts.name: Techniques of Differentiation
concepts.description: Computational methods for finding derivatives including power rule, product rule, quotient rule, chain rule, and implicit differentiation, applied to various function types.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to use linear approximation to estimate function values and understand the relationship between differentials and small changes.
concepts.name: Linear Approximation and Differentials
concepts.description: Using the tangent line to approximate function values near a known point, with applications to estimation and error analysis in scientific and engineering contexts.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to find equations of tangent lines and normal lines to curves using derivatives.
concepts.name: Tangents and Normal Lines
concepts.description: Geometric applications of derivatives to find equations of tangent lines and normal (perpendicular) lines to curves at given points, with problem-solving applications.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to use derivatives to solve related-rates problems involving quantities that change with respect to time.
concepts.name: Related Rates
concepts.description: Application of derivatives to problems where multiple quantities change with respect to time, requiring the chain rule to relate their rates of change.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply the chain rule to differentiate composite functions.
concepts.name: Chain Rule
concepts.description: The differentiation rule for composite functions that expresses the derivative of f(g(x)) as the product of derivatives, essential for differentiating nested function structures.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to use implicit differentiation to find derivatives of implicitly defined functions.
concepts.name: Implicit Differentiation
concepts.description: Technique for finding derivatives when y is defined implicitly as a function of x rather than explicitly, applied to curves not expressible as y = f(x).

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to analyze extreme value functions and find maxima and minima of single-variable functions.
concepts.name: Extreme Values of Functions
concepts.description: Identification and classification of maximum and minimum values of functions, including absolute and relative extrema, critical points, and the Extreme Value Theorem.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to understand and apply mean value theorems to analyze function behavior and prove mathematical statements.
concepts.name: Mean Value Theorems
concepts.description: Fundamental theoretical results including Rolle's Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem that establish relationships between average and instantaneous rates of change, with applications to proving properties of functions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to analyze concavity of a function and use complete function analysis to sketch graphs of polynomials and rational functions.
concepts.name: Concavity and Curve Sketching
concepts.description: Analysis of second derivative to determine concavity, inflection points, and comprehensive curve sketching combining information about increasing/decreasing behavior, extrema, and concavity.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to use derivatives to solve optimization problems in science and engineering contexts.
concepts.name: Optimization Problems
concepts.description: Application of calculus to find maximum or minimum values in practical scenarios, involving mathematical modeling, constraint identification, and critical point analysis.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to express integration as an anti-derivative of a function and evaluate basic indefinite integrals.
concepts.name: Antiderivatives and Indefinite Integration
concepts.description: The concept of integration as the inverse operation of differentiation, including basic integration formulas and the notation and properties of indefinite integrals.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to identify and apply different techniques to solve indefinite integrals including substitution, parts, and partial fractions.
concepts.name: Techniques of Integration
concepts.description: Advanced methods for evaluating integrals including integration by substitution, integration by parts, integration by partial fractions, and trigonometric substitutions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to understand Riemann sums, define definite integrals, and apply their properties.
concepts.name: Riemann Sums and Definite Integrals
concepts.description: Definition of the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums, properties of definite integrals, and the connection between area and integration.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate definite integrals and understand the relationship between derivatives and integrals.
concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.description: The central theorem linking differential and integral calculus, establishing that differentiation and integration are inverse operations and providing methods to evaluate definite integrals using antiderivatives.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply definite integrals to solve problems in science and engineering beyond simple area calculations.
concepts.name: Applications of Definite Integrals
concepts.description: Problem-solving using definite integrals for quantities such as areas, volumes, arc lengths, work, centers of mass, and other accumulated quantities in physical and geometric contexts.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to implement definite integrals to find area under a curve and between curves.
concepts.name: Area Under Curves
concepts.description: Calculation of areas bounded by curves, lines, and axes using definite integrals, including regions between two curves and signed area interpretation.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate improper integrals and determine their convergence or divergence.
concepts.name: Improper Integrals
concepts.description: Evaluation of integrals with infinite limits of integration or unbounded integrands, including convergence and divergence tests and their applications.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to represent and analyze straight lines in three-dimensional space using various equation forms.
concepts.name: Straight Lines in Three-Dimensional Space
concepts.description: Equations and properties of lines in R³ including parametric, symmetric, and vector equations, direction vectors, and relationships between lines.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to write and interpret equations for planes in three-dimensional space and analyze their geometric relationships.
concepts.name: Equations of Planes
concepts.description: Representation of planes in three-dimensional space using normal vectors, scalar and vector equations, and analysis of plane relationships including intersections and angles.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to identify domains and ranges of functions, recognize and sketch graphs of common functions, and interpret functions arising in applied contexts.
concepts.name: Functions and Their Representations
concepts.description: Mathematical relations that assign exactly one output to each input, studied through their definitions, domain-range relationships, and graphical representations including standard function families.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to perform arithmetic operations on functions, compute and simplify compositions of functions, and decompose composite functions.
concepts.name: Function Operations and Composition
concepts.description: Arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) performed on functions, and the composition operation where the output of one function becomes the input of another.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to predict and sketch transformed graphs from parent functions, identify transformations from equations, and write equations from transformed graphs.
concepts.name: Graph Transformations
concepts.description: Systematic modifications of function graphs including translations (shifts), reflections, symmetry operations, and vertical/horizontal stretches and compressions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to algebraically test for and identify even and odd symmetry, and exploit these symmetries in integration and graphing.
concepts.name: Even and Odd Functions
concepts.description: Function symmetry classifications where even functions satisfy f(-x) = f(x) (symmetric about y-axis) and odd functions satisfy f(-x) = -f(x) (symmetric about origin).

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to analyze polynomial and rational functions, identify zeros and asymptotes, and understand their limiting behavior.
concepts.name: Polynomial and Rational Functions
concepts.description: Algebraic functions defined by polynomial expressions and ratios of polynomials, including their algebraic properties, graphical behavior, and end behavior characteristics.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate trigonometric functions, sketch their graphs with proper period and amplitude, and apply trigonometric identities.
concepts.name: Trigonometric Functions
concepts.description: The six basic trigonometric functions (sine, cosine, tangent, cotangent, secant, cosecant) defined through unit circle and right triangle relationships, with their periodic properties and graphs.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to determine if functions are invertible, compute inverse functions, and relate graphs of functions and their inverses through reflection across y = x.
concepts.name: Inverse Functions
concepts.description: Functions that reverse the action of another function, requiring one-to-one correspondence, with methods for finding inverses algebraically and graphically.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate inverse trigonometric functions, understand their restricted domains, and use them to solve for angles in applied problems.
concepts.name: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
concepts.description: Restricted-domain inverses of trigonometric functions including arcsine, arccosine, and arctangent, with their domains, ranges, and applications in solving trigonometric equations.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to manipulate exponential and logarithmic expressions, solve exponential and logarithmic equations, and model continuous growth processes.
concepts.name: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
concepts.description: Functions of the form a^x and their inverses log_a(x), including their algebraic properties, graphs, and natural base e, with applications to growth and decay.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate left-hand and right-hand limits, determine when two-sided limits exist, and analyze function behavior near discontinuities.
concepts.name: One-Sided and Two-Sided Limits
concepts.description: Directional limits from left and right sides of a point, with conditions for existence of the overall limit requiring agreement of both one-sided limits.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate infinite limits, identify horizontal asymptotes, and describe end behavior of functions using limit notation.
concepts.name: Limits at Infinity and End Behavior
concepts.description: Behavior of functions as inputs grow without bound, describing horizontal asymptotes and long-term trends of polynomial, rational, and transcendental functions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to locate vertical asymptotes by analyzing limits, describe function behavior near asymptotes, and distinguish them from removable discontinuities.
concepts.name: Vertical Asymptotes
concepts.description: Points where function values grow without bound, identified through infinite limits, representing points of discontinuity where functions are undefined.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute limits using algebraic manipulation, handle indeterminate forms, and evaluate limits of piecewise functions at transition points.
concepts.name: Computing Limits Algebraically
concepts.description: Techniques for evaluating limits of polynomials, rational functions, and piecewise-defined functions through direct substitution, factoring, rationalization, and analyzing one-sided cases.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply the Intermediate Value Theorem to prove existence of solutions, locate roots approximately, and understand its requirements.
concepts.name: Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.description: Theorem guaranteeing that continuous functions take on all intermediate values between endpoints, with applications to locating roots and proving existence of solutions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply the Squeeze Theorem to evaluate difficult limits, particularly the limit of sin(x)/x as x approaches zero.
concepts.name: Squeeze Theorem
concepts.description: Limit theorem stating that functions bounded between two others approaching the same limit must also approach that limit, essential for proving fundamental trigonometric limits.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute derivatives using the limit definition, interpret derivatives as rates of change, and understand the derivative as a function.
concepts.name: The Derivative
concepts.description: The instantaneous rate of change and slope of tangent line, defined as the limit of difference quotients, forming the derivative function that gives slopes at all points.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to determine where functions are differentiable, understand differentiability implies continuity, and identify non-differentiable points geometrically.
concepts.name: Differentiability
concepts.description: Conditions under which derivatives exist, including the relationship between differentiability and continuity, and failure of differentiability at corners, cusps, and vertical tangents.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute higher-order derivatives, interpret their meanings in physical contexts, and use them in Taylor approximations.
concepts.name: Higher-Order Derivatives
concepts.description: Successive differentiation producing second derivatives, third derivatives, and beyond, with interpretations as acceleration and rates of change of rates of change.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to differentiate products and quotients of functions correctly, and recognize when to apply these rules versus expanding first.
concepts.name: Product and Quotient Rules
concepts.description: Differentiation formulas for products and quotients of functions, extending basic rules to handle multiplication and division of differentiable functions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to differentiate all trigonometric functions, apply these derivatives to related rates and optimization, and use the cyclic pattern of sine and cosine derivatives.
concepts.name: Derivatives of Trigonometric Functions
concepts.description: Differentiation formulas for sine, cosine, tangent, and other trigonometric functions, derived from limit definitions and essential for modeling periodic phenomena.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to differentiate composite functions using the chain rule, handle multiple compositions, and apply it to implicitly defined functions.
concepts.name: The Chain Rule
concepts.description: Fundamental rule for differentiating composite functions, stating that the derivative of a composition is the product of derivatives of the outer and inner functions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to differentiate exponential and logarithmic functions, apply logarithmic differentiation to complex products and powers, and solve related rates problems.
concepts.name: Derivatives of Logarithmic and Exponential Functions
concepts.description: Differentiation formulas for a^x, e^x, log_a(x), and ln(x), including logarithmic differentiation technique for products, quotients, and powers.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to differentiate inverse trigonometric functions and integrate resulting forms, recognizing their derivatives in integration problems.
concepts.name: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
concepts.description: Differentiation formulas for arcsine, arccosine, arctangent, and other inverse trigonometric functions, derived using implicit differentiation.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply L'Hôpital's Rule to evaluate difficult limits, recognize applicable indeterminate forms, and transform other forms to apply the rule.
concepts.name: L'Hôpital's Rule
concepts.description: Method for evaluating indeterminate limits of form 0/0 or ∞/∞ by comparing derivatives of numerator and denominator, extending to other indeterminate forms.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to construct sign charts for derivatives, determine intervals of monotonicity and concavity, and sketch accurate graphs using derivative information.
concepts.name: Analysis of Functions Using Derivatives
concepts.description: Using first and second derivatives to determine intervals of increase and decrease, concavity, and classify critical points as relative maxima or minima.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to find absolute extrema on closed intervals by comparing critical values and endpoints, and understand when extrema are guaranteed to exist.
concepts.name: Absolute Extrema and Extreme Value Theorem
concepts.description: Maximum and minimum values of functions on closed intervals, with the Extreme Value Theorem guaranteeing their existence for continuous functions on closed bounded intervals.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to translate applied optimization problems into mathematical models, solve for optimal solutions, and verify their results.
concepts.name: Applications of Extrema
concepts.description: Optimization problems from geometry, physics, economics, and other fields where maximum or minimum values are sought, modeled and solved using calculus techniques.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to approximate areas using Riemann sums, understand the definite integral as a limit of sums, and apply integral properties.
concepts.name: The Definite Integral and Area
concepts.description: Riemann sums and their limit defining the definite integral, solving the area problem through summation and limit processes, with properties of definite integrals.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to find antiderivatives of basic functions, understand the constant of integration, and verify antiderivatives by differentiation.
concepts.name: The Indefinite Integral and Antiderivatives
concepts.description: The reverse process of differentiation, finding functions whose derivative is given, with constant of integration and basic integration rules corresponding to differentiation formulas.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to identify and execute appropriate substitutions, change limits for definite integrals, and recognize patterns requiring substitution.
concepts.name: Integration by Substitution
concepts.description: The chain rule in reverse, transforming integrals through change of variable to match basic antiderivative forms, applicable to both indefinite and definite integrals.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply both parts of the Fundamental Theorem, understand the relationship between area functions and derivatives, and evaluate definite integrals efficiently.
concepts.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.description: The central theorem linking differential and integral calculus, showing that differentiation and integration are inverse operations and enabling evaluation of definite integrals using antiderivatives.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to apply integration by parts to products of algebraic and transcendental functions, use tabular methods for repeated integration by parts, and choose u and dv effectively.
concepts.name: Integration by Parts
concepts.description: Integration technique derived from the product rule, transforming integrals of products into potentially simpler integrals through strategic choice of parts.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to integrate powers of sine and cosine, products of trigonometric functions, and apply half-angle and double-angle identities in integration.
concepts.name: Integration of Trigonometric Functions
concepts.description: Techniques for integrating powers and products of trigonometric functions using identities, reduction formulas, and strategic substitutions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to recognize integrals suitable for trigonometric substitution, execute the substitutions, and convert back to original variables using reference triangles.
concepts.name: Trigonometric Substitution
concepts.description: Integration technique using substitutions based on trigonometric identities to eliminate radicals of forms sqrt(a^2-x^2), sqrt(a^2+x^2), and sqrt(x^2-a^2).

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to represent vectors in 3D coordinates, perform vector operations, and find magnitudes and directions of vectors.
concepts.name: Vectors in Three Dimensions
concepts.description: Directed quantities in 3D space represented by components, with operations of addition, scalar multiplication, magnitude, and direction cosines.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute dot and cross products, interpret their geometric meanings, and apply them to find angles, projections, and orthogonal vectors.
concepts.name: Dot Product and Cross Product
concepts.description: Two fundamental vector multiplications: the scalar (dot) product measuring parallelism and projecting vectors, and the vector (cross) product producing perpendicular vectors measuring area and orientation.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to compute scalar and vector projections, find orthogonal projections onto lines and planes, and apply projections to geometric problems.
concepts.name: Vector Projections
concepts.description: Decomposition of vectors into parallel and perpendicular components relative to another vector, with applications to distances and orthogonal bases.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to write equations of lines in 3D, determine if lines intersect or are skew, and find distances from points to lines.
concepts.name: Lines in Three-Dimensional Space
concepts.description: Parametric and symmetric equations describing straight lines in 3D using point and direction vector, with applications to intersections and distances.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to write plane equations, find angles between planes and lines, compute distances from points to planes, and find line-plane intersections.
concepts.name: Planes in Three-Dimensional Space
concepts.description: Equations of planes using point and normal vector, including standard form, normal form, and relationships between planes such as parallelism, perpendicularity, and intersection.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to identify whether a function has an inverse, find the inverse of a given function, and verify that two functions are inverses using composition.
concepts.name: Properties of Functions and Their Inverses
concepts.description: Understanding the fundamental characteristics of functions including one-to-one and onto properties, and how to determine and work with inverse functions algebraically and graphically.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to analytically determine the domain and range of a given function and express them in proper interval notation.
concepts.name: Domain and Range of Functions
concepts.description: Determining the set of valid input values (domain) and possible output values (range) for various types of functions including polynomial, rational, trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to find the general anti-derivative of polynomial, exponential, and basic trigonometric functions.
concepts.name: Integration as Anti-derivatives
concepts.description: Understanding indefinite integration as the reverse process of differentiation, including basic integration rules and the constant of integration.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to decompose proper rational functions into partial fractions and integrate the resulting simpler terms.
concepts.name: Integration by Partial Fractions
concepts.description: Technique for decomposing rational functions into simpler fractions that can be integrated, including handling of proper/improper fractions and repeated or irreducible quadratic factors.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to evaluate definite integrals using the Fundamental Theorem, apply the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals, and understand differentiation of integral-defined functions.
concepts.name: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.description: Understanding definite integration as a limit of Riemann sums, and applying both parts of the Fundamental Theorem to evaluate definite integrals and establish the relationship between differentiation and integration.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to model physical situations using derivatives, solve related rates problems, and interpret derivatives in applied contexts.
concepts.name: Derivatives and Their Applications
concepts.description: Applying differentiation to solve practical problems in science and engineering, including rates of change, related rates, and geometric interpretation as slope of tangent lines.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to translate real-world optimization problems into mathematical models, find critical points, classify extrema, and interpret solutions in context.
concepts.name: Optimization Using Derivatives
concepts.description: Finding maximum and minimum values of functions to solve practical optimization problems, including identifying critical points, applying first and second derivative tests, and verifying global extrema on closed intervals.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to set up and evaluate definite integrals to find areas of regions bounded by curves, including cases requiring subdivision or integration with respect to y.
concepts.name: Area Under a Curve Using Definite Integrals
concepts.description: Computing the area between curves and bounded regions using definite integration, including handling of regions bounded by multiple curves and vertical/horizontal elements.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to find critical points, test intervals for sign of the first derivative, and describe where a function is increasing or decreasing.
concepts.name: Function Behavior Analysis: Increasing and Decreasing Functions
concepts.description: Using the first derivative to determine intervals where functions are increasing or decreasing, and identifying critical points where extrema may occur.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to determine intervals of concavity, find points of inflection, and use concavity information to refine curve sketching.
concepts.name: Concavity and Points of Inflection
concepts.description: Using the second derivative to analyze concavity of functions, identify points of inflection where concavity changes, and relate concavity to the shape of curves.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to find critical points, apply derivative tests to classify extrema, and determine absolute extrema on specified domains.
concepts.name: Relative and Absolute Extrema of Functions
concepts.description: Locating and classifying local and global maximum and minimum values using first and second derivative tests, and evaluating extrema on closed and open intervals.

concepts.learning_outcomes: After studying this, students will be able to systematically analyze all features of a function and produce complete, accurate sketches showing key characteristics.
concepts.name: Curve Sketching of Polynomial Functions
concepts.description: Synthesizing information from domain, intercepts, symmetry, asymptotes, first and second derivatives to create accurate graphs of polynomial and rational functions.
